# 2 Chronicles Chapter 16 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** In the thirty-sixth year of Asa's reign, King Baasha of Israel marched against Judah and fortified Ramah to prevent anyone from entering or leaving Asa's territory.

**2** Asa then took silver and gold from the treasuries of the LORD's temple and the royal palace and sent them to Ben-hadad king of Aram, who was ruling in Damascus.

**3** "Let there be a treaty between us," he said, "as there was between our fathers. Here — I'm sending you silver and gold. Break your treaty with King Baasha of Israel so he'll pull back from me."

**4** Ben-hadad agreed and sent his army commanders against the cities of Israel. They conquered Ijon, Dan, Abel-maim, and all the supply cities of Naphtali.

**5** When Baasha heard about it, he stopped fortifying Ramah and abandoned the project.

**6** Then King Asa brought all of Judah to carry away the stones and timber Baasha had been using at Ramah, and he used them to build up Geba and Mizpah.

**7** At that time the seer Hanani came to King Asa of Judah and said, "Because you relied on the king of Aram instead of on the LORD your God, the army of the king of Aram has slipped out of your grasp.

**8** Weren't the Cushites and Libyans a massive army with huge numbers of chariots and horsemen? Yet when you relied on the LORD, He handed them over to you.

**9** For the eyes of the LORD search the whole earth to strengthen those whose hearts are fully committed to Him. You have done a foolish thing. From now on you will be at war."

**10** Asa was furious with the seer and threw him in prison, putting him in the stocks. Asa also brutally oppressed some of the people at that time.

**11** Everything Asa did, from beginning to end, is recorded in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.

**12** In the thirty-ninth year of his reign, Asa developed a severe disease in his feet. Even in his illness, he did not seek the LORD's help but only the help of doctors.

**13** Asa died in the forty-first year of his reign.

**14** They buried him in the tomb he had cut for himself in the City of David. They laid him on a bed covered with spices and various blended perfumes, and they built a huge fire in his honor.


---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **16:7-8**: The tragic irony of Asa's story: the man who once trusted God against a million soldiers now pays a pagan king to handle a much smaller problem. Faith, the Chronicler warns, can atrophy.

- **16:9**: "The eyes of the LORD search the whole earth to strengthen those whose hearts are fully committed to Him" — one of the most powerful verses in the Bible. God is actively looking for people to bless. Asa used to be that person. He isn't anymore.

- **16:12**: "He did not seek the LORD but only doctors" — the Chronicler isn't anti-medicine. He's anti-autonomy. Asa's real disease isn't in his feet; it's in his heart. He's stopped needing God.


— PNEUMA
